newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Gazprom rules out direct Bulgaria supply.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom rules out direct Bulgaria supply.

text.p: Russia's Gazprom will supply natural gas to Bulgaria through its joint companies Topenergy and Overgas Inc, but not directly from the producer, a Gazprom supervisory board member was quoted as saying.
"Without a joint company, natural gas will not arrive," Bogdan Budzuliak, who is in Sofia for talks with government officials, told Douma daily in an interview published on Wednesday.
Budzuliak said Gazprom had prepared long-term deals with Topenergy and Overgas for natural gas supplies to Bulgaria.

"A deal will be signed for gas supplies from Gazexport to Topenergy. This means that in the long term there will be two suppliers on the Bulgarian market, which are Overgas with two billion cubic metres and Topenergy with a contract for 3.5 billion," he said.
Budzuliak said a German firm would supply another 500 million cubic metres "but it will work on your market until the year 2000". He did not name the firm.
Gazprom has a 50 percent stake in Topenergy and Overgas.
Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said last week Bulgaria would insist on receiving Russian gas directly from producer Gazprom or its exporting arm Gazexport.
He said gas deliveries through an intermediary increased the purchase price by $10-15 per 1,000 cubic metres and Bulgaria was being charged $99 per 1,000 cubic metres.

Bulgarian gas distributor Bulgargas, which represents the interests of the state, has 25.1 percent in Topenergy. The powerful conglomerate Multigroup holds 8.5 percent in the joint company and its subsidiary Overgas also holds 8.5 percent. The remainder is held by Bulgarian banks and private companies.

Bulgaria and Russia signed in April in Moscow an intergovernmental agreement on the transit of Russian gas to the Balkans and construction of new pipelines, but Budzuliak said the Bulgarian government seemed reluctant to implement the agreement.
"We are convinced that everything possible is being done to prevent it being realised," Budzuliak said.
The Russian and Bulgarian governments still have to set the gas supply price and transit fees.
Topenergy said in May that it was ready to start the construction of a second gas pipeline between the borders of Romania and Turkey for transporting Russian gas to Turkey.
"Work until now has created good perspectives for increasing gas supplies to Turkey by two billion cubic metres," Budzuliak said.

He said a 10 km gas pipeline should be constructed and Topenergy would receive for it a $40 million credit for Gazexport. A compressor station for regulating gas volumes will be constructed near Provadia in northeastern Bulgaria.
Bulgargas is at odds with Topenergy over transit fees. Budziliak said $4 per 1,000 cubic metres sought by Bulgaria was a very high price.
Deputy Prime Minister Evgeni Bakardzhiev said on Tuesday after talks with Budzuliak that he hoped common ground would be found soon. Bakardzhiev is expected to visit Moscow on July 15.
